statement: Build a single-file HTML, CSS and JavaScript event page for the Bengaluru JS Meetup in November, with schedule, speakers, RSVP, venue and map, code of conduct and sponsor logos. Where a fact is missing, the page shows a clearly marked placeholder instead of invented content.
audience: People who may attend the Bengaluru JS Meetup in November and need its schedule, speakers, RSVP, venue and code of conduct.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file; CDN libraries are allowed; no build step.
No invented facts: no sample speaker names, talk titles, times, dates, venue, sponsor names or links.
Every missing fact is shown as visible 'To be announced' text or a clearly marked placeholder.
No attendee data is collected or processed on the page.
No third-party map that needs an API key or an account.
rules: Missing content uses real section structure with 'To be announced' text only (CEO decision 1).
RSVP is a link-out button to an external page, shown as a marked placeholder until a link is supplied (CEO decision 2).

The map is an OpenStreetMap map via Leaflet from a CDN, plus a text address. Until the venue is confirmed it shows a Bengaluru city view with no pin and a 'venue to be announced' note (CEO decision 3).
Missing facts and the RSVP link are tracked as open inputs and do not block done (CEO).
done_when: The deliverable is one HTML file with its CSS and JavaScript inline, any libraries loaded from a CDN, and no build step or local dependencies.
The page title and main heading contain 'Bengaluru JS Meetup' and the page text states that the event is in November.
The file contains a Schedule section whose time slots and talk entries all read 'To be announced', with no sample times or talk titles.
The file contains a Speakers section whose entries all read 'To be announced', with no personal names.
The file contains an RSVP section with a button or link marked as a placeholder, and the file has no form element and no input fields.
The file contains a Venue section with a text address reading 'To be announced' and a visible 'venue to be announced' note.
The file loads Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles and renders a map centred on Bengaluru with no marker, and contains no Google Maps embed or API key.
The file contains a Code of Conduct section with a heading and a marked placeholder stating that the text is to be announced.
The file contains a Sponsors section with logo slots marked 'To be announced', with no sponsor names and no image sources.

Every missing fact in the file appears as visible 'To be announced' text or a marked placeholder, and the file contains no invented speaker names, talk titles, times, exact dates, venue names or sponsor names.
open_inputs: Venue name, full address and exact map coordinates
